meta: François Gérard painted the miniaturist Jean-Baptiste Isabey with his four-year-old daughter and a dog on a Louvre staircase in 1795.
about: Jean-Baptiste Isabey and His Daughter is a portrait of 1795 by François Gérard. It shows his fellow painter Isabey, a celebrated painter of miniatures, with his four-year-old daughter Alexandrine and a pet dog on the Henry IV staircase at the Louvre. Gérard was a pupil of Jacques-Louis David and became a leading portraitist under Napoleon and the Restoration. The painting was shown at the Salon of 1796, and the Louvre acquired it in 1852.

meta: Hendrik van Demmeltraadt sits leaning on a walking stick in a velvet cap in a portrait by Jean Augustin Daiwaille, about 1810.
about: Hendrik van Demmeltraadt, who lived from 1736 or 1737 to 1819, is shown half-length, seated with a hand resting on a walking stick and a velvet cap on his head. Jean Augustin Daiwaille painted the portrait, which the catalog dates to 1810.

meta: Clothing is handed out to the needy in an Italian square in Michael Sweerts's Clothing the Naked, 1646.
about: On a square in an Italian city, clothing is given out to the needy, and a boy in a hat helps another man dress. The picture is part of a series on the seven works of mercy. Michael Sweerts painted it in 1646, and the Rijksmuseum bought it with support from its photo sales committee.

meta: Two Spanish women with fan and shawls walk across a square past soldiers in Constantin Guys's In a Spanish Town, about 1840.
about: Two Spanish women, seen from the side and back, walk in a public square with their heads in profile. The one at the right wears a gray skirt and a black shawl over her head. The other has a blue and white striped dress and black shawl, with an elaborate headdress and a fan. A group of soldiers and Spanish architecture are in the background. Constantin Guys made the picture around 1840.

meta: A ceiling painting with putti playing with flowers and hunting with dogs, by Elias van Nijmegen, 1695.
about: This ornamental ceiling painting has putti in the corners playing with flowers and hunting with dogs. It is one half of a pair, and it probably comes from the palace of the Frisian stadtholders in Leeuwarden. Elias van Nijmegen painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1695.

meta: Caravaggio's Boy Bitten by a Lizard, which exists in two versions, one in Florence and one in London, from about 1594 to 1596.
about: Boy Bitten by a Lizard exists in two versions, both believed to be authentic Caravaggios, one in the Fondazione Roberto Longhi in Florence and the other in the National Gallery in London. Both date from 1594 to 1596. Who posed is debated. One theory names Mario Minniti, Caravaggio's companion, and Michael Fried proposes a disguised self-portrait, since the boy's hands resemble a painter's holding a palette.

meta: Small birds, butterflies and a lizard among leaves and mushrooms at the foot of a tree, painted by Melchior d'Hondecoeter in 1668.
about: Several small birds, butterflies and a lizard are among leaves and mushrooms at the foot of a tree. Melchior d'Hondecoeter painted this forest floor in 1668, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Adam and Eve flee the angel with the flaming sword in Cornelis van Poelenburch's Expulsion from Paradise, 1646.
about: Adam and Eve flee from paradise, hiding their nakedness in shame. An angel with a flaming sword drives them out, and cows graze at the left. Cornelis van Poelenburch painted the Expulsion from Paradise in 1646.

meta: Willem IV, Prince of Orange-Nassau, in armor in a miniature by Jean-Étienne Liotard of 1755.
about: Willem IV, Prince of Orange-Nassau, who lived from 1711 to 1751, is shown in bust length turned to the right and wearing armor. The portrait is part of the Rijksmuseum's collection of portrait miniatures. Jean-Étienne Liotard made it in 1755.

meta: The head of an old woman with closed eyes and loose hair, a study by Matthijs Maris of 1856.
about: This is a study of the head of an old woman in three-quarter view turned to the right, with closed eyes and loose hair. Matthijs Maris made it in 1856, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A decorative ewer covered in floral motifs, with a woman and child on the handle, designed by Jean-Charles Delafosse, about 1760.
about: The ewer fills the whole sheet. Its decoration includes a half figure of a woman and a child on the lower part of the handle at the left, and a satyr and a woman on the rim. Floral and vegetal motifs cover its whole surface. Jean-Charles Delafosse made the design around 1760.

meta: Courtesans bathe, wash laundry and comb hair in a women's bathhouse in a painting by Kitao Shigemasa.
about: In Edo-period Japan, bathing was a communal activity, and bathhouses were popular places to socialize. The women here, most likely courtesans, do many tasks besides bathing, such as washing laundry and combing each other's hair. Two women near the back are reading a book, and one holds her hand to her face as if shocked by what she reads, or perhaps to whisper in the other's ear. Kitao Shigemasa painted the scene.

meta: A door handle design with a dragon, flying putti and a seated Hercules, with alternative suggestions, by Jean Le Pautre, about 1650.
about: On the recto, left and right halves of different designs are joined. The left motif has a dragon and a flying putto with foliage, and the right has a half-figure and a putto with foliage framing a roundel with a seated Hercules. The verso has a dragon's forepart on a scrollwork bracket at the left, and a flying putto and an eagle at the right, with two putti supporting the keyhole below. Jean Le Pautre made the design.

meta: Lorenzo Lotto's Madonna and Child with Saint Peter Martyr and a Donor, his first known work, painted in Treviso in 1503.
about: Lorenzo Lotto's first known work, an oil on panel of 1503, was painted early in his time in Treviso. The date is inscribed on the back in a 16th-century hand. It was probably ordered by Bishop Bernardo de' Rossi, perhaps as an ex voto for escaping a murder attempt planned for 29 September 1503. It probably came to Parma with Rossi in 1524 and later entered the Farnese collection, then moved to Naples in 1760, and it is now in the Museo di Capodimonte.

meta: A heart-shaped auricular cartouche topped by a winged woman, plate 28 of Christoph Jamnitzer's New Grotesque Book, about 1600.
about: An ornamental cartouche is made of auricular, cartilage-like forms in the shape of a heart, topped by a half-length winged female figure. At either side similar volute forms rest on a grasshopper at the left and a tortoise at the right. It is plate 28 from the Neüw Grotteßken Buch by Christoph Jamnitzer.

meta: Dancing figures before the Doges' Palace in another section of Martin Engelbrecht's peep-show The Carnival of Venice, about 1730.
about: This section of a peep-show print shows dancing figures, with the Palace of the Doges on the right and the library on the left. The campanile of Saint Mark's, the Mint and a church also appear. The right edge of each section is taped to a folding cardboard mount, in which some parts act as cross members. Martin Engelbrecht made it around 1730.
